extracted.intended_audience: senior theoretical scientists / faculty considering applying to the Simons Investigators programs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and program-level criteria for the Simons Investigators awards (Mathematics, Physics, Astrophysics, Theoretical CS, MMLS, Math+X), including target candidate profile, appointment/renewal terms, program objectives and how to submit an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target candidate profile — outstanding theoretical scientists
rubrics_metrics.description: "Simons Investigators are outstanding theoretical scientists who receive a stable base of research support from the foundation, enabling them to undertake the long-term study of fundamental questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is aimed at outstanding theoretical researchers; the award provides a stable base of research support to enable long-term fundamental work. (Implied selection focus: demonstrated excellence in theoretical research.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Career stage — most productive years
rubrics_metrics.description: "The intent ... is to support outstanding theoretical scientists in their most productive years, when they are establishing creative new research directions, providing leadership to the field and effectively mentoring junior scientists."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be in a career phase characterized by high productivity and the potential to establish new research directions, lead the field, and mentor junior scientists — these are explicit program aims used to identify appropriate candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research originality and direction — establishing creative new research directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Program emphasis on applicants who are "establishing creative new research directions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors investigators proposing or already pursuing novel, creative directions in theoretical research rather than incremental work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership and mentorship — providing leadership and effectively mentoring junior scientists
rubrics_metrics.description: Program intent includes supporting scientists who are "providing leadership to the field and effectively mentoring junior scientists."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of leadership in the field and a record (or clear plan) of mentoring junior researchers are important evaluation dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment length and renewal condition
rubrics_metrics.description: "A Simons Investigator is appointed for an initial period of five years. Renewal for an additional five years is contingent upon the evaluation of scientific impact of the Investigator."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are five-year appointments with possible five-year renewal; renewal decisions are explicitly based on an evaluation of the Investigator's scientific impact during the initial term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field/program-specific eligibility — supported disciplines (Mathematics, Physics, Astrophysics, Theoretical Computer Science, MMLS, Math+X)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs named: "Simons Investigators in Mathematics, Physics, Astrophysics and Computer Science," "Simons Investigators in Mathematical Modeling of Living Systems (MMLS)", and "Math+X Investigators."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each named program targets investigators in the listed disciplines or interdisciplinary areas; applicants should align with one of these program areas when applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: MMLS objective — mathematical/theoretical approaches to life sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: "This program aims to help the research careers of outstanding scientists working on mathematical and theoretical approaches to topics in the life sciences. A Simons Investigator in MMLS is appointed for five years."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MMLS specifically evaluates investigators whose work applies mathematical/theoretical methods to life-science problems; suitability for this subprogram depends on that focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math+X objective — encourage novel collaborations between mathematics and other fields
rubrics_metrics.description: "This program encourages novel collaborations between mathematics and other fields in science or engineering by providing funds to professors to establish programs at the interface between mathematics and other fields of science or engineering."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Math+X selects for investigators proposing or leading interdisciplinary programs at the math/other-field interface; proposals should emphasize collaboration and program-building at that interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission procedure — use proposalCENTRAL
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Simons Foundation uses an electronic grants submission process. All interested grant applicants must submit their applications online through proposalCENTRAL."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement: applicants must apply via proposalCENTRAL. After logging in, navigate to the grant opportunities tab, filter by 'Simons Foundation' and select the appropriate Simons Foundation opportunity from the list. (Follow proposalCENTRAL workflow; failure to use this portal would violate application instructions.)
